title: Factoring the Difference of Perfect Squares

lesson.title: Difference of Perfect Squares
intro: A difference of perfect squares has the form \(a^2 - b^2\).
Look for terms that are both perfect squares and separated by subtraction.
This pattern is useful for factoring expressions quickly.

workedExample.aiHint: Check whether both terms are perfect squares and the operation is subtraction.

questions.prompt: When factored, the expression \(x^3 - 36x\) is equivalent to
questions.explanation: First factor out \(x\): \(x(x^2 - 36)\). Then factor the difference of squares: \(x(x+6)(x-6)\).

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to \(a^8 - b^6\)?
questions.explanation: Rewrite each term as a perfect square: \(a^8 = (a^4)^2\) and \(b^6 = (b^3)^2\).
